research_question: Can an information-junction model inspired by p-n semiconductor dynamics reduce SAT search transitions without hiding exponential cost in time, energy, precision, communication, or preprocessing?
claim_boundary: No result in this repository proves P=NP, polynomial worst-case scaling, or physical equivalence between semiconductor p-n junctions and complexity classes P/NP.

experiments.headline: At 3-SAT n=48, median solved steps were 128 for WalkSAT and 36.5 for Junction; both solved 8/8.
At 3-SAT n=64, solve rates were 15/16 WalkSAT and 16/16 for both Junction variants; median solved steps were 155, 55, and 42 respectively.
experiments.negative_result: At 3-SAT n=32, tunneling regressed median steps from 38 to 48 because escape activation was too aggressive.

full_json.scope: summary rows; detailed trial records are reproducible by rerunning the code

next_gate.name: adaptive depletion-depth detector
required_controls: wall-time, memory, energy and communication accounting
next_gate.failure_condition: If the apparent step advantage disappears under matched initialization, standard benchmarks, incremental implementations, or resource-normalized accounting, the Junction advantage claim must be reduced or rejected.
